subject: Temporary burst window & handshake for MedLytics pilot — autoscale exception request
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary burst window & handshake for MedLytics pilot — autoscale exception request

Hi team,

Following the sync with MedLytics this morning, they're asking for a short-term burst window during their pilot next week to run high-concurrency inference for a live health-check workload. Their asks are:

- 2x sustained concurrency for up to 3 hours/day for three days (pilot days: 26–28 May)
- Guaranteed low-latency lane for those windows (p95 target unchanged)
- A documented handshake so we can flip the routing and fallback quickly if capacity or QoS degrades

I realize this conflicts with our standard autoscale/eviction rules. Can we treat this as an autoscale exception with a dedicated temporary slice and a defined runbook? Specific asks:

1) Ops: can you confirm whether a 2-hour contiguous burst (or a 3-hour staggered window) is feasible given the current pool occupancy?
2) Product: do we need model-variant gating or token-limits to keep p95 latency within SLO?
3) Sales/Legal: can we capture the burst window in the mutual action plan and waiver the normal reservation lead-time?

I'm attaching MedLytics' proposed schedule. If we can get an ops-runbook draft + capacity commitment by end of day Friday (21 May) I will confirm with the customer and lock the pilot slots.

Thanks —
Jordan
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: medlytics_proposed_burst_schedule.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 12:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary burst window & handshake for MedLytics pilot — autoscale exception request

Jordan —

Thanks for the heads up and the schedule. High level: we can do a timeboxed exception but we need an explicit rollback trigger (error rate or spike in tail latency) and a one-button fallback plan for the customer-facing routing.

Questions / constraints:
- Pool usage on 26–28 currently ~78% midday; any additional reserved slice will need explicit eviction tolerance.
- Can we restrict the pilot workload to a model-quantization profile (faster path) to reduce GPU slot pressure?

I'll draft a minimal ops runbook with the handshake steps (enable slice, apply routing tag, monitor, rollback conditions) and attach it here. For approvals I'll need: owner for rollback, SRE on-call that can be paged, and a timeboxed SLA waiver.

I'm attaching the runbook draft for comments. If you can confirm the SRE contact and sign-off timeline we can include this in the MAP to operations.

Kimberly
Head of Dedicated Capacity Ops
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: ops_runbook_v2.pdf (document)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 10:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary burst window & handshake for MedLytics pilot — autoscale exception request

Quick capacity note from infra:

We ran a short simulation against the pool schedule. Given current reservations and expected autoscale headroom, we can't safely commit to a continuous 3-hour contiguous 2x capacity without impacting other pilots unless we do one of the following mitigations:

A) Provide a reserved temporary slice of 6x slots but only allow a 2-hour contiguous window per day (we carve the slice but gate usage to the window) — this is the cleanest from an eviction perspective.
B) Route MedLytics traffic to a cheaper, lower-latency-compatible model variant for aggressive quantization during burst windows (would require product sign-off on degradation risk).
C) Allow staged bursts (3 x 1-hour windows) to reduce peak simultaneous concurrency.

Operationally we can implement A today if Product and Sales agree to the time bounding, and Legal okays the waiver. I've attached a short run of the simulation results and linked INF-3456 where I posted the capacity chart. Please route SRE contact (pager) so we can include them in the runbook.

-Aditya
Product Infrastructure Manager
Redwood Inference
[Inline: simulation_summary.png]
Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3456

Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary burst window & handshake for MedLytics pilot — autoscale exception request

Thanks — this is helpful. Action items and next steps:

1) Kimberly: finalize the ops runbook with explicit rollback triggers and include the SRE pager contact (due EOD 21 May).
2) Aditya: proceed with option A (reserved temp slice + timebound window) and post the exact slice size and gating controls to INF-3456 (due EOD 21 May).
3) Tessa: capture the timebound waiver language in the MAP and confirm Legal route (I'll loop contracts@medlytics.ai once we have the runbook).

Sanjay — cc'ing you so you're aware of the constraints. If MedLytics can accept a 2-hour contiguous burst window (we'll offer a second 1-hour contingency window), we can lock this in and ship the runbook + SLA waiver by Monday. Please confirm whether MedLytics prefers contiguous or staged windows.

Jordan Blake
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
